title: CP Rail The Canadian.jpg
credit: CP Rail - The Canadian Uploaded by Skeezix1000
description: Railway lands in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. CP Rail's flagship train "The Canadian" departs Union Station for Sudbury where it will meet up with the section from Montreal. From thence, it will follow a southern route along the north shore of Lake Superior to Thunder Bay. From there it will proceed to Winnipeg, Regina, Calgary and Vancouver.

title: Toronto skyline 1973 (fixed).jpg
description: Taken from the Toronto Islands before the construction of the CN Tower. This photo appears to have been inadvertently inverted horizontally when it was scanned. Flipped horizontally via the Preview image editing tool on Mac.

title: CN Tower footings 1973.jpg
credit: CN Tower footings Uploaded by Skeezix1000
description: CP Rail's "The Canadian" arrives from Vancouver passing the CN Tower in its initial construction phase. The footings are in place and the concrete slip form is starting to build the tower. All the railway infrastructure except for the lines into Toronto Union Station and the CP roundhouse have been demolished.

title: CN Tower Construction Base.jpg
description: Constructing the base of CN Tower, Toronto

title: Uncompleted CN Tower from Island Yacht Club.jpg
credit: Uncompleted CN Tower from Queen City Yacht Club Uploaded by Skeezix1000
description: In this view of the CN Tower, the slip form concrete work is now complete. There is a crain in position at the top of what will become the skydeck. This begins construction of the Skypod, Skydeck and the communications antennae.

title: Toronto skyline from Wards Island (1).jpg
credit: Toronto Skyline from Ward's Island Uploaded by Skeezix1000
description: At this time, the concrete work for the CN tower had been completed. The Island Yacht Club is in the foreground

title: CN Tower, Skycrane Approaches (3805193162).jpg
by: Robert Taylor from Stirling, ON, Canada
description: Sikorsky S-64 Skycrane Helicopter nicknamed "Olga" approaches the CN Tower with another section of the broadcast tower. The tower was manufactured in sections then hoisted into place by the skycrane.
